A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RetroAttention work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and algorithms, equations, figures and results can be matched despite reformatting and expansion.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy, perplexity, attention-overlap and latency experiments, including supplementary measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds larger-model evaluations, LongBench results, ArkVale comparisons and further diagnostic measurements.

M1.justification: The supplementary-attention computation, output cache, retrospective mask and deeper-layer KV updates remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. The ArkVale experiments exercise the existing generic page-selector interface without documenting a new RetroAttention procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on 12 LongBench tasks spanning single-document and multi-document QA, summarization, code completion and few-shot QA. This substantially extends coverage to long-input, generally short-output scenarios while retaining the original long-generation, reasoning and language-modeling benchmarks.

E2.justification: The original Full Attention, StreamingLLM, TOVA and Quest comparisons remain. V2 additionally evaluates Quest with top-k selection reuse in Table 4 and ArkVale with and without RetroAttention in Table 9; ArkVale was only discussed in v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2.5-14B/32B evaluations, a selection-reuse control refreshing every two steps, throughput profiling across batch sizes 1–16 and contexts 32k–128k, and token-level normalized Levenshtein similarity. These are substantial additional evaluation configurations; the original main-table settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing window/budget analyses with tests of selection-reuse failure, attention mass recovered by successive updates, batch-dependent throughput and memory exhaustion, and page overlap across additional datasets. Tables 4–6 and Figure 8 substantially strengthen investigation of the mechanism and practical operating limits.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or new seed-based uncertainty estimates. The reasoning evaluations retain the same 8, 2 and 1 samples per question documented in v1 Appendix D and v2 Appendix F.1.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 and reasoning table are numerically unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results for larger models, ArkVale, reuse, throughput and LongBench. For example, Table 2 reports Qwen2.5-14B mean GSM8K accuracy of 77.6 versus Quest's 73.2. V2 Table 4 also inconsistently prints a CSQA mean of 63.0 for scores whose unchanged Table 1 mean is 60.3.

T1.justification: The attention and output-merging equations, smooth-QKV approximation assumption, and arithmetic-intensity and memory derivations are retained. Their renumbering and relocation introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same central claim: retrospective updates mitigate accumulated attention errors without increasing the KV budget and with negligible overhead. The headline claims of up to 1.6-fold effective exposure and 21.9% accuracy improvement remain; the contribution bullets reorganize existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains saturation through diminishing supplementary attention mass and limited LongBench benefits through short generation lengths. It also distinguishes agreement with full attention from correctness, provides window-selection guidance, and explicitly identifies full-KV GPU residency and batch-size limits. These materially clarify mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and a reproducibility statement describing source code, documentation and evaluation scripts. It explicitly discloses greedy LongGenBench decoding and its prompt-construction source. These improve documented reproducibility without establishing changes to the retained implementation or decoding procedure.

R1.justification: V2 adds the LongBench and LServe references and explicitly contrasts retrospective correction with cache-selection reuse in Section 2.2 and Appendix B. Most prior-work discussion, including the comparison with Rectified Sparse Attention, is retained.

P1.justification: Most original prose remains. V2 revises the contribution list and motivational narrative, moves Related Works after the experiments, subdivides experimental and appendix sections, and adds acknowledgment, ethics and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column conference format, rearranges Figure 1, and adds a prompt-example panel to Figure 2. It introduces numerous evaluation tables and the expanded overlap Figure 8. The original linear-layer Figure 8 is retained as Figure 9.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation across model families and cache selectors through Qwen14B/32B and ArkVale experiments. New throughput measurements and LongBench evaluations clarify deployment limits and where benefits diminish, while code-access information supports reproducibility. New reporting errors temper this improvement: Table 4's CSQA mean conflicts with Table 1, and Table 5's 0.650 entry contradicts the stated 4–7% range. These localized inconsistencies do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and applicability guidance.
